record.paper_title: Causal Machine Learning: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Causal reinforcement learning uses many overlapping Markov decision process, partially observable Markov decision process, confounded-MDP, causal-POMDP, contextual-MDP, and hidden-parameter-MDP formalisms. Which of these formalisms can be unified or compared rigorously, and when should practitioners use each?

evidence.quote: Unification of Formalisms: Due to the parallels between causality and reinforcement learning and the lack of maturity at the intersection of both, we fear redundancy among papers, i.e., an analogy of reinventing the wheel [317] taking place.
We suggest that future work compares the applicability of different formalisms more rigorously and possibly unifies them.

In the literature, we notice a myriad of MDP formalisms proposed for that type of setup: MDP with Unobserved Confounders [318], Confounded MDPs [319], Causal POMDPs 1 [237], Causal POMDPs 2 [243] (they are not the same formulation), Causal MDPs [232], and discrete MDPs (a universe, Sec. 7.4) [250].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following decision-process formalisms used in sequential decision making under uncertainty and/or unobserved confounding:

1. Markov Decision Process (MDP): a tuple (S, A, P, R, γ) where S is a state space, A an action space, P(s' | s, a) a transition kernel, R(s, a) a reward function, and γ ∈ [0,1) a discount factor.

2. Partially Observable MDP (POMDP): an MDP augmented with an observation space O and observation kernel Z(o | s, a), where the agent only sees observations o ∈ O rather than the underlying state s.

3. MDP with Unobserved Confounders / Confounded MDP: an MDP in which transitions and rewards depend on an unobserved confounding variable U that may also influence the behavioral policy generating offline data, so that P(s' | s, a, u) and R(s, a, u) are governed by a structural causal model with latent U.

4. Causal POMDP (type I): a POMDP whose dynamics are specified by a structural causal model with explicit intervention semantics on actions and a do-calculus over observations.

5. Causal POMDP (type II): an alternative formulation in which the observation/state generative process is given by a causal Bayesian network and the policy may perform soft or hard interventions on a designated subset of nodes.

6. Causal MDP: an MDP whose state-transition and reward mechanisms are determined by a structural causal model over a finite set of endogenous variables, with actions corresponding to interventions on those variables.

7. Contextual MDP (CMDP): a family of MDPs {M_c}_{c ∈ C} indexed by an observed context c drawn from a distribution over C, where each M_c has its own transition and reward functions.

8. Hidden-Parameter MDP (HiP-MDP): a family of MDPs indexed by a latent parameter θ ∈ Θ drawn from a prior, where transitions P_θ and rewards R_θ depend on the unobserved θ which is fixed within an episode.

Problem. Provide a rigorous mathematical framework that:

(a) Defines each of the eight formalisms above as instances or quotients of a single unifying object (for example, a structural causal influence diagram together with a designated set of intervenable nodes, observable nodes, and latent nodes).

(b) Establishes precise reductions or equivalences between pairs of these formalisms, specifying for each pair whether one is a strict special case of the other, whether they are equivalent under a canonical embedding, or whether they are genuinely distinct, and proving the corresponding statements.

(c) Identifies, for each formalism, necessary and sufficient structural conditions (in terms of identifiability of causal effects, observability of confounders, stationarity of latent parameters, and dependence of dynamics on context) under which it is the appropriate model class, in the sense that any decision problem satisfying those conditions admits an optimal policy expressible within that formalism but not within strictly smaller ones in the hierarchy.

Produce either such a unification together with the reductions and characterizations in (a)–(c), or prove an impossibility result showing that no such common framework exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open direction for future work in causal reinforcement learning. Subsequent surveys and works on causal RL (e.g., Bareinboim et al.'s causal RL program, recent 2023–2025 surveys) continue to enumerate these formalisms without providing a single unifying framework with rigorous reductions among MDPs with unobserved confounders, causal POMDPs (multiple variants), causal MDPs, contextual MDPs, and HiP-MDPs. No published result is found that solves (a)–(c) jointly, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys multiple causal RL formalisms (confounded MDPs, causal POMDPs, etc.) and lists unification of formalisms as an open challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Unification of overlapping causal RL formalisms remains an outstanding open direction.

status_evidence.title: Towards Causal Reinforcement Learning (Bareinboim)
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research program continues to introduce new causal decision-process formalisms without a single unified reduction theorem.
status_evidence.snippet: Talks and tutorials present separate frameworks (MDPUC, causal MDP, causal POMDP) rather than a unified hierarchy.
